scope: Snapshot A/B, LK scalar tag values and the corrected picture of the fault address inside the MD image. Read-only device access; no firmware payload was dumped.

image.adds: scalar LK tag values in the boot log (no new sysfs, no payload)

snapshot_ab.question: does a stale NVRAM snapshot explain the MD fault?
snapshot_ab.difference: 11 files, all updated by the vendor stack after the first extraction
snapshot_ab.conclusion: identical outcome with both snapshots, so the snapshot age is not the cause; the fault is deterministic across three runs with two different snapshots and three different images

lk_scalars.source: boot log, allowlisted single-u32 tags only

interpretation.image_size: md1img is 33,471,260 bytes (31.92 MiB), matching the md1rom partition header size, so the loaded image spans the whole bank0 head
interpretation.fault_addresses: with the MD view base 0x90000000, pc is image+0x1823b66 (24.14 MiB) and the faulting address is image+0xd18620 (13.10 MiB); both are inside the 31.92 MiB image, so this is not an access past the loaded image
interpretation.cache_md_base: md1_smem_cahce_offset is 0x8000000, so the cached bank4 MD view is 0x40000000 + 0x8000000 = 0x48000000, exactly the value the driver publishes and exactly the vendor formula
interpretation.mpu_table: md_mpu_num is 9 and the tag is 216 bytes, so an entry is 24 bytes; the vendor struct _mpu_cfg is 20 bytes, which confirms the LK table is not that struct and must not be applied as if it were

not_done: no modem firmware payload or code was dumped; only headers and scalar tags were read
the MD's read-only/writable segment split is not obtainable from kernel-side metadata, because LK owns that layout
next_observation_point: the vendor trace continues with UM12_005 after MF04_003, while this firmware faults instead; everything the AP supplies up to that point has been shown exact, so further progress needs MD-internal evidence rather than another AP-side guess
